title: Dataverse: create agent users with Microsoft Entra agent identity

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing promises auditing of every read, but Dataverse auditing explicitly excludes retrieve operations. The Conditional Access instructions also use the wrong selection and API condition, Power Platform administrators need environment-level elevation, and the no-cost rating is not supported.

claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The general availability date is August CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "August CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Agents can receive dedicated least-privilege Dataverse security roles based on their intended capabilities.
claims.quote: This feature enables agents to be provisioned as Dataverse agent users with dedicated, least-privileged security roles based on their intended capabilities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Agents can perform permitted tasks autonomously or on behalf of users.
claims.quote: This feature ensures agents have only the access required to perform tasks autonomously or on behalf of users.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes auditing of agent-driven actions and traceability of Dataverse data access and changes.
claims.quote: By using identity-based role assignment and full auditing of agent-driven actions, organizations can enforce security and compliance policies across both human users and AI agents while maintaining traceability of data access and changes within Dataverse environments.

claims.where: What's changing: every create, read, update and delete; summary: full auditing
claims.claim: Having its own identity means every create, read, update and delete performed by the agent is audited.
claims.quote: Furthermore, auditing doesn't support retrieve operations or export operations. In addition to Dataverse auditing, you can turn on Dataverse and model-driven apps activity logging to log data retrieve operations and export operations.
claims.fix: Remove the unconditional every-operation promise. State that configured Dataverse auditing records supported changes; reads and exports require separate activity logging, whose licensing and production-environment qualifications must also be stated. Attribute the roadmap's broader auditing description to the roadmap.

claims.claim: Agent users are added to individual Dataverse environments through the Power Platform admin center and assigned security roles.
claims.quote:
Choose the agent user from the search list, and then select Add to add the agent.
On the Manage security roles page, select a security role for your agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn still labels Dataverse agent users as preview despite the launched roadmap status.
claims.quote:
Create an agent user (preview)
[This section is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]
This is a preview feature.

claims.where: What's changing: third kind of principal; Why it matters: two existing patterns
claims.claim: Before agent users, there were exactly two patterns for giving agents Dataverse access: people and application users.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users create API programmatically security roles license capacity column security migration; Dataverse agent application users migrate. Opened create-users and agent-users; neither establishes this exhaustive history.
claims.fix: Replace the historical enumeration with 'Agent users provide an identity option alongside regular users and application users.' Remove 'third kind' and 'the two existing patterns'.

claims.where: Why it matters: running as the maker
claims.claim: Using a person's delegated access ties the agent's available access to that person's permissions.
claims.quote: It also means a change to the person's access affects what the agent can do through that delegated path.
claims.fix: Cite this article and replace 'leaves when they do' with the documented wording that changes to the person's access affect the delegated path.

claims.where: Why it matters: running as an application user
claims.claim: Application-user access usually means a broad role shared by many integrations.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent application users migrate; Dataverse agent users security roles. Opened create-users and read security-roles-privileges results; no passage establishes that broad shared roles are the usual application-user pattern.
claims.fix: Replace the asserted usual behaviour with conditional analysis: 'If integrations share an application user, separating their identities can make ownership and role reviews clearer.'

claims.where: Why it matters: application-user audit trails
claims.claim: Application-user audit trails cannot distinguish one automation from another.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent application users migrate; Dataverse agent users security roles. Opened create-users and manage-dataverse-auditing; neither states that application-user audit trails inherently cannot distinguish automations.
claims.fix: Qualify this as a risk of sharing the same identity, not a limitation of all application users, or remove it.

claims.claim: Agents with Entra agent identities can be inventoried in Agent 365.
claims.quote: The comprehensive agent inventory, including agents without a Microsoft Entra agent identity, is available in Agent 365.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Conditional Access can govern Entra agent identities.
claims.quote: Conditional Access policies can block authentication and token issuance of agent identities.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Entra sign-in logs capture agent identity activity.
claims.quote: Agent identity activities are captured in Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs

claims.claim: An administrator can disable an agent identity centrally in Entra.
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities.
Select the agent identity you want to disable then select Disable.

claims.claim: Agent users can be granted access to column-secured Dataverse data.
claims.quote:
Column-level security configurations are organization-wide and apply to all data access requests.
Use a column security profile to grant user or team members the following permissions
claims.fix: Cite this general Dataverse user control and explain that column security profiles govern secured-column access; security-role assignment alone is not the column-security configuration.

claims.claim: Agent identities are a distinct Entra identity type.
claims.quote: Agent identities are a distinct identity type in Microsoft Entra ID, designed for AI agents with classification, metadata, and security controls tailored to agentic workloads.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Entra access reviews can be used to review agent identities' access.
claims.quote: Use access reviews to periodically verify that agent identities still need the access they have.
claims.fix: Cite this agent-specific applicability statement rather than leaving the access-review recommendation without a supporting reference.

claims.claim: Agent identities can hold Entra role assignments that administrators should monitor.
claims.quote: Each agent identity has a service principal or a user in Microsoft Entra ID, and it can be assigned certain Microsoft Entra roles.
claims.fix: Cite this article and retain its qualification that many high-privilege roles are blocked for agent identities.

claims.claim: The agent identity uses Entra Agent ID authentication and token handling.
claims.quote: You use the agent identity blueprint to create each agent identity. Request an access token from Microsoft Entra using your agent identity blueprint

claims.claim: Existing agents using application users will not migrate automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent" "migrate" "application users". Opened create-users and agent-users; neither documents automatic migration or a guarantee that migration will not occur.
claims.fix: Replace with 'Microsoft has not documented migration from existing application users at the time of writing (November 2026).' Keep any inventory recommendation explicitly as the wiki's advice.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Dataverse change auditing requires environment, table and column auditing configuration.
claims.quote: First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: storage and indirect costs
claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume Dataverse log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.claim: API capacity consumed by an agent user is charged against the environment as usual.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user API request capacity non licensed users pooled tenant. Read api-request-limits-allocations and api-limits-overview excerpts; agent-user allocation is not specified and the nonlicensed pool described is tenant-level.
claims.fix: Remove the environment-level API allocation assertion. Say that the feature documentation does not specify agent-user request-entitlement allocation, and cite the general request-limit guidance separately without assigning an undocumented pool.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio usage remains subject to its platform licensing and consumption rules.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.
claims.fix: Cite the Copilot Studio billing article and use its current term 'Copilot Credits' instead of 'credits or messages'. Do not imply that these are a separate charge for provisioning a Dataverse agent user.

claims.claim: Using Agent 365 governance brings its own licensing requirements.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 E7, which includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite, to provide governance of user and agent identities.
Microsoft Agent 365 license paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.
claims.fix: Cite this source and specify the published governance license alternatives. Distinguish paid governance from merely viewing the Agent 365 inventory, which the cited registry-convergence article says needs no specific license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Dataverse agent-user documentation does not state a separate agent-user licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent users" "license"; Dataverse agent users licensing storage API capacity Copilot Studio credits Agent 365. Opened create-users and agent-users; neither states a dedicated agent-user license or included entitlement.

claims.claim: The Power Platform Administrator role alone suffices to create agent users and assign their Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: Global admins, Power Platform admins, and Dynamics 365 service administrators must complete another step before they can perform activities requiring access to Dataverse. They must elevate themselves to the System Administrator role in the environment where they need access.
claims.fix: State that Dataverse security management requires the environment System Administrator role or equivalent privileges. Power Platform administrators must first self-elevate to System Administrator in that environment; cite this article.

claims.claim: An environment System Administrator can manage Dataverse user security roles.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.
claims.fix: Add this role-reference article to sources.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agents can receive Entra agent identities for this identity model.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio integrates with Microsoft Entra Agent ID so that agents created in Copilot Studio can automatically receive an Entra agent identity

claims.where: Scope: other platforms that issue Agent IDs
claims.claim: Entra agent identities are also issued by platforms beyond Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Agents created in Microsoft Entra Agent ID or using the latest iterations of systems like Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, and Security Copilot are created with agent identities.

claims.claim: Government cloud dates for this Dataverse agent-user feature are not published in the checked material.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent users" "Government". Read roadmap record and opened create-users and agent-users; no government-cloud date is stated.

select Manage.
select Environments.
choose an environment.
select Settings.
Expand Users + permissions, and then select Agents.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row API
claims.claim: No agent-specific API equivalent for adding a Dataverse agent user and assigning its roles is documented in the checked sources.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent user" "API"; "Dataverse" "agent users" "API" "create" provisioning. Opened create-users and agent-users; Graph agentUser and Dataverse application-user results do not document this Dataverse agent-user operation.

claims.claim: The Entra creation path is Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities > New agent identity (Preview).
claims.quote:
Browse to Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities.
Select New agent identity (Preview).

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row API
claims.claim: Microsoft Graph v1.0 supports Create agentIdentity with POST.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity
claims.fix: Replace the operation title with the actionable call 'POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity'. The lifecycle tutorial still illustrates /beta/; note that difference if retaining both references.

claims.claim: The sign-in blocking path ends New policy > Users, agents or workload identities > Agents.
claims.quote:
Under Assignments, select Users, agents or workload identities.
Under Include, select All agent identities
Under Exclude, select None
claims.fix: For agent-identity authentication, replace the path with 'Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy > Assignments > Users, agents or workload identities > Include > All agent identities'. Describe selecting all resources and the Block grant separately; remove the invented final 'Agents' step.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: third row API
claims.claim: POST /identity/conditionalAccess/policies blocks agent identities by putting them in the policy's users condition.
claims.fix: Use 'POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies' with conditions.clientApplications.includeAgentIdServicePrincipals for agent identities. The users condition with includeUsers: ["AllAgentIdUsers"] is a different policy for agents acting as users; label that separately if intended. Keep report-only rollout advice.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: third row note
claims.claim: The documented Conditional Access policy requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.
claims.quote: Applying Conditional Access policies in your tenant requires the Microsoft Entra ID P1 license.

claims.claim: The auditing path is Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings.
claims.quote:
Select Manage in the navigation pane.

Select Settings.
Expand Audit and logs and then select Audit settings.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth row API
claims.claim: Updating the organization table's IsAuditEnabled setting through the Dataverse Web API controls environment auditing.
claims.quote:
IsAuditEnabled isauditenabled Is Auditing Enabled | Boolean | Whether auditing is enabled for the environment
Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment.
claims.fix: Make the conceptual instruction concrete: 'PATCH /api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>) with {"isauditenabled": true}'. Use the logical Web API property name isauditenabled, not the SDK schema name IsAuditEnabled.

claims.where: Governance controls: Dataverse side is portal-only

claims.fix: Replace 'is portal-only' with 'The agent-user creation article documents the portal flow; no agent-specific API equivalent is documented in the checked sources as of November 2026.' Do not extend that absence to all Dataverse role-assignment APIs.

claims.where: Governance controls: agent users overview covers licensing and limits
claims.claim: The linked agent-users overview covers licensing and limits.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent users" "license"; Dataverse agent users licensing storage API capacity. Opened the complete agent-users overview: it contains preview notices, identity integration, a creation link and an unsupported-application-user note, not licensing or limits.
claims.fix: Replace with 'The agent users overview describes the preview identity model and links to the creation procedure; dedicated licensing and limits are not stated there.'

claims.claim: The checked documentation does not resolve agent-user-specific licensing for restricted Dynamics 365 tables.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent users" "license". Opened agent-users and create-users; read data-platform-entity-licenses#restricted-tables. General app-user licensing is documented, but no agent-user-specific interpretation is stated.

claims.where: Open questions: platforms beyond Copilot Studio
claims.claim: The Dataverse agent-user documentation does not enumerate supported external agent platforms beyond its Copilot Studio integration example.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent user" "other" "platforms". Opened agent-users and create-users; they give the Entra identity prerequisite and Copilot Studio example, not a Dataverse binding compatibility matrix.

claims.claim: The checked sources do not document environment-group templates for agent-user security-role assignments.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "agent users" "environment groups" role assignment. Opened create-users and agent-users; read database-security-configure results. No agent-user environment-group role-template procedure was found.

claims.claim: A cost rating of none is justified while licensing is unknown and indirect costs are identified.
claims.quote:
cost: "none"
licensing:
  model: "unknown"
Indirect: role design time; audit storage growth if auditing is enabled broadly.
rationale: None stated. Uses existing Dataverse and Entra capabilities; licensing notes unpublished.
claims.fix: Do not infer inclusion from missing licensing notes. Set cost to low for the known configuration/admin effort and state that feature-specific licensing is not published; distinguish any separately chosen metered agent platform or paid governance capability. The standard reserves none for explicitly documented inclusion.

claims.where: Governance guidance: turn on auditing for tables; controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers the checklist's table- and column-auditing configuration.
claims.quote:
Turn on Dataverse auditing for the environments and tables agents will touch
controls[3].ui ends at environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Audit settings; no table/column auditing row is present.
claims.fix: Add a maker-surface table/column auditing row sourced to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-dataverse-auditing#configure-auditing-for-one-or-more-tables-and-columns-in-power-apps, including its System Administrator/System Customizer prerequisite.

claims.where: Governance guidance: add identities to Entra access reviews; controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers the checklist's Entra access-review control.
claims.quote:
Add agent identities to the scope of your Entra access reviews.
The table contains agent creation, identity lifecycle, Conditional Access and Dataverse auditing, but no access-review row.
claims.fix: Add an agent-access-review row, with the appropriate documented review surface and licensing, or remove the instruction to configure that control and retain only general manual access-review advice.

claims.where: Governance guidance: monitor Entra sign-in logs; controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers the checklist's agent sign-in monitoring control.
claims.quote:
Monitor Entra sign-in logs for agent identities and alert on unexpected locations or volumes.
No sign-in-log control appears in the table.
claims.fix: Add a sign-in monitoring row sourced to https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/manage-agent-identities-admin#sign-in-and-audit-logs: Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs, with agent filters and the documented Reports Reader prerequisite.

claims.where: Governance guidance: define standard security roles; controls
claims.claim: The controls table covers creating the checklist's standard custom agent security roles.
claims.quote:
Define a small set of standard agent security roles
The first control assigns existing roles during agent creation; no security-role design/configuration control is listed.
claims.fix: Add a security-role configuration row sourced to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/database-security-configure: Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > Security roles.

claims.claim: Agent-user Dataverse access is admin-opt-in because an environment agent user and its role assignment must be configured.
claims.quote: For agents that require data access to a Dataverse environment, an Entra agent user must be created and associated with the agent identity so that appropriate security roles can be assigned to enable access to Dataverse APIs and data within the environment.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Dataverse storage
claims.claim: Data stored in Dataverse remains subject to ordinary Dataverse storage-capacity accounting.
claims.quote: Dataverse - Database capacity: Tracks structured data stored directly in Dataverse, including table rows, metadata, and relational data
claims.fix: Cite the Dataverse capacity article for the general storage rule; do not describe an agent-specific storage entitlement that this source does not establish.
